mechanism_narrative: An increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases but the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the next 20 trading days, this hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% indicates monetary easing, which may stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS falls below 0.5% but the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in at least 55% of the next 60 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) coupled with a decrease in GDP (GDPC1) suggests supply chain constraints, which may negatively impact corporate profitability and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases and GDPC1 decreases but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 35% of the next 20 trading days, this hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases but the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in at least 50% of the next 5 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% in a late-cycle expansion may indicate labor market tightness, leading to inflationary pressures and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is below 4% but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 45% of the next 60 trading days, this hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) coupled with a low unemployment rate (UNRATE) may indicate stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases and UNRATE remains low
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL increases and UNRATE remains low but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the next 20 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.2% indicates extreme monetary easing, which may lead to increased borrowing and spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS falls below 0.2% but the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in at least 55% of the next 5 trading days, this hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong economic activity, which may lead to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases but the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the next 60 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.
